articles.title: Ahora sí, Ounahi se marcha al Panathinaikos
articles.standfirst: Los griegos pagan al Girona unos 15 millones más uno en variables y un 20% de un futuro traspaso
articles.summary: Los griegos pagan al Girona unos 15 millones más uno en variables y un 20% de un futuro traspaso
articles.body: Quedarse a Azzedine Ounahi en Segunda quizás era un lujo para el Girona. Pese a que el mercado de fichajes en España está cerrado, no ha podido decir que no a una nueva ofensiva del Panathinaikos para hacerse con los servicios del marroquí. Los griegos finalmente pagarán unos 15 millones de euros más uno en variables y el 20% de una futura venta, algo que queda lejos de la cláusula del futbolista, de 25 millones, pero mucho más que lo que pagaron los catalanes el verano pasado al Olympique de Marsella (6 millones). De la cuantía que ingrese del traspaso, el Girona tendrá que abonar un 20% a los franceses, que se guardaron ese porcentaje al firmar el traspaso en las últimas horas del mercado estival del 2025. El club blanquirrojo pierde un activo muy importante, algo que se sabía desde el descenso a Segunda y el hecho que el futbolista compitiera a buen nivel en el Mundial con Marruecos. Pese a esto, los clubes interesados en Ounahi no alcanzaban las pretensiones de los gerundenses, que a medida que pasaban los días han rebajado su postura de fuerza para ingresar una buena cantidad, el doble de lo que pagaron. El mercado en Grecia se cierra el próximo 15 de setiembre, pero el Panathinaikos debe presentar antes de esta madrugada la lista de jugadores que competirán en la Conference League, por lo que la última ofensiva de los griegos ha sido inmediata a la oferta rechazada ayer por el Girona. Ounahi ya no entrenó ni ayer ni hoy y pasó el reconocimiento médico en Atenas para firmar el contrato con un equipo en el que ya jugó la temporada 2024-25, antes de venir a Cataluña, en calidad de cedido por el Marsella.

articles.title: Ángel Haro explica el adiós de Pablo García: "Es rotundamente falso que el club lo haya empujado"
articles.standfirst: El presidente del Betis confirma que su traspaso al Racing fue a petición del futbolista
articles.summary: El presidente del Betis confirma que su traspaso al Racing fue a petición del futbolista
articles.body: Ángel Haro, presidente del Betis, quiso explicar con detalle cómo se produjo la salida del canterano Pablo García al Racing de Santander, una aclaración motivada por las duras críticas recibidas por parte de mucho aficionados que vincularon este traspaso con la necesidad de generar límite salarial para firmar a Dani Ceballos. Una situación que el máximo mandatario verdiblanco negó rotundamente. "Primero quiero aclarar, en base también a alguna de las preguntas que se han hecho dando por hecho que la salida de Pablo tenía que ver con la llegada de Dani, que nada más lejos de la realidad. Estamos hablando de que Pablo tenía una ficha del filial, de lo que es la plantilla no inscribible; por tanto, no afectaba en absoluto, además de tener una ficha relativamente baja. Incluso la plusvalía que se ha producido tampoco afecta al límite, teniendo en cuenta que tienes un límite donde hay una plusvalía estimada en función de la media de los últimos tres años, y hasta que no llegues a esa cantidad cualquier plusvalía no te computa. Por tanto, desde un punto de vista ni deportivo ni económico afectaba a la llegada de Dani Ceballos. De alguna manera se ha ido comentando que era necesaria la salida de Pablo para la llegada de Dani y es algo totalmente falso", explicó Haro. El presidente fue todavía más contundente al referirse a quién tomó la iniciativa para buscar una salida: "Con respecto a la salida de Pablo, al que le deseo lo mejor, también es rotundamente falso que el club lo haya empujado. El club no ha empujado a nada. Desde hace unas tres semanas, Pablo entendía que era su momento de salir, así nos lo ha hecho llegar por activa y por pasiva, utilizando términos como 'os ruego que me dejéis salir', 'creo que es mi momento, tengo que salir', 'no voy a tener minutos aquí'". Según el relato de Haro, inicialmente apareció una propuesta del Hull City, que el Betis descartó por sus condiciones, y posteriormente fueron los representantes del jugador quienes trasladaron el interés del Racing. "El Betis ha escuchado ofertas. Llegó una primera oferta del Hull City que veíamos que no era adecuada, sobre todo por la forma de pago. Se quedó un poco esto más frío y el último día del mercado sus agentes nos hablan de que el Racing está interesado, que por favor actuemos y negociemos. Negociamos, llegamos a un acuerdo. Seguimos pensando que Pablo tiene proyección, por eso nos quedamos con el 50% del jugador; además, nos quedamos con un derecho de tanteo". Haro entiende que las lágrimas del futbolista en su despedida no contradicen esta versión. "Por un lado, su carrera deportiva le pedía salir y, por otro, da pena salir del equipo de sus amores. Las dos cosas son compatibles. Respeto la salida. Él vino a recoger sus cosas y rompió a llorar, pero nosotros no hemos provocado la salida, sino simplemente hemos respetado lo que quería el jugador y hemos llegado a un acuerdo con un club que incluso ellos mismos nos han puesto por delante". El presidente insistió además en que la necesidad de minutos era lógica por la competencia existente en la plantilla: "Entiendo que Pablo quiera minutos; tiene por delante jugadores como Antony y tenemos dos delanteros. Es comprensible que quiera tener minutos. Hemos comprendido la situación, no hemos tenido prisa, pero desde luego no lo hemos empujado a salir". Respecto a las cantidades de la operación y al supuesto interés del Arsenal, Haro añadió: "Creo que las cifras son razonables. El Racing no lo pone encima de la mesa el club, lo trae el propio jugador y sus agentes diciendo que era donde quería irse. Los agentes manifestaron que podría haber una opción de que el Arsenal lo quisiera para cederlo a un equipo español, pero el Arsenal no se ha puesto en contacto con nosotros, ni hemos tenido ninguna comunicación por su parte".

articles.title: Haro sale al paso de las críticas a la planificación: "El derrotismo no se lo compro a nadie"
articles.standfirst: El presidente defiende la inversión y Fajardo reconoce que faltó mano dura con las salidas
articles.summary: El presidente defiende la inversión y Fajardo reconoce que faltó mano dura con las salidas
articles.body: El cierre del mercado veraniego de fichajes ha dejado una sensación de insatisfacción en una parte de la afición del Betis, especialmente por la ausencia de un nuevo pivote defensivo, una posición para la que incluso Manuel Pellegrini había reclamado públicamente un refuerzo, y por la marcha a última hora del canterano Pablo García mientras otros futbolistas como Nelson Deossa o Iker Losada continuaban en el club. Ángel Haro, presidente, y Manu Fajardo, director deportivo, respondieron a esas críticas en su balance de la planificación. El máximo mandatario del club verdiblanco defendió la inversión y el nivel de la plantilla construida: "El Betis es el cuarto equipo que más ha invertido en esta temporada de fichajes y tiene la quinta mayor plantilla de LaLiga, muy cerquita del cuarto y mucho más lejos del sexto". Haro admite que había margen de mejora, pero rechaza el clima negativo generado alrededor del cierre del mercado. «¿Que se podían hacer las cosas mejor? Siempre se pueden hacer mejor, pero tenemos un Betis en un estado envidiable: un campo que vamos a terminar y un Betis en Champions después de 21 años. La gestión de las expectativas y el sentimiento depende de cada uno, pero el derrotismo no se lo compro a nadie". Fajardo sí realizó autocrítica, especialmente respecto a las salidas que no pudieron concretarse: "Creo que es necesaria la autocrítica. Al final, cuando termina un mercado hay que analizar, sentarse y valorar qué se ha hecho bien y qué no se ha terminado de hacer del todo bien. Para estar a la altura de un club como el Betis, todos tenemos que ser autocríticos y exigentes con nosotros mismos". Y concretó uno de los errores que considera que deben corregir: "Entiendo que a veces, a la hora de dar salidas a jugadores, hay que afrontarlo desde una postura o dureza que a lo mejor no hemos tenido en distintos momentos del mercado; de eso se aprende". Respecto al pivote defensivo, el director deportivo dejó clara cuál fue la apuesta del Betis durante el verano: "Nosotros, desde la Dirección Deportiva, siempre hemos tenido claro que la apuesta en el pivote defensivo era Facundo Bernal; quizás traer a un jugador de la jerarquía de Fofana podría pisar la trayectoria de Facundo en el Real Betis. Con la complementariedad de Marc Roca, entendíamos que esa posición estaba cubierta". Una postura que no necesariamente coincidía con la de Pellegrini. Fajardo reconoció la existencia de debate interno: "Manuel, desde su experiencia, puede demandar perfiles concretos; nosotros, desde la nuestra, podemos tener un punto de vista diferente, pero de ese intercambio de criterios el mayor beneficiado es la entidad". Y dejó una frase significativa sobre lo que podría haber sucedido si el Betis hubiera conseguido liberar alguna ficha: "Tenemos jugadores en la plantilla que pueden ocupar esa demarcación y no se sabe si, de haber tenido fichas disponibles, hubiésemos ido a por un perfil más defensivo o de mayor equilibrio". Pese a las críticas, Fajardo considera que la plantilla ha dado un salto: "Consideramos que hemos mejorado considerablemente la plantilla respecto a la temporada pasada". Y asegura aceptar el descontento del beticismo: "Si no aceptas la crítica, no podrías estar aquí sentado".

articles.title: El Sabadell, campeón de la Copa Cataluña tras batir al Barça Atlètic
articles.standfirst: El equipo de Ferran Costa alimentó su gran momento con un ajustado 2-1
articles.summary: El equipo de Ferran Costa alimentó su gran momento con un ajustado 2-1
articles.body: El Sabadell saborea uno de los momentos más felices de su historia moderna. Este miércoles celebró una nueva alegría con la conquista de su segundo título de la Copa Cataluña tras un trabajado triunfo contra el Barça Atlètic (2-1). Ferran Costa, técnico arlequinado, ya avisó en la previa que quería el título para seguir viviendo "alegrías para el recuerdo" y planteó un once titular con nueve jugadores que ya han sido titulares en las tres primeras jornadas de LaLiga Hypermotion. El Sabadell, dos categorías superior a su rival, se adelantó en el 4' con un gol de Niko Gioacchini, el autor del tanto de la ilusionante victoria del sábado ante el Almería. El Barça Atlètic perdió por lesión al extremo belga Jesse Bisiwu, fichado por ocho millones del Brujas. Dejó el césped en camilla tras un preocupante pisotón en el tobillo. El equipo de Juliano Belletti dio un paso adelante tras el descanso y empató por mediación de Hafiz Gariba, pero el Sabadell continuó coleccionando ocasiones hasta conseguir el 2-1 en el 87'. Fue Yanis Rahmani, en un saque de esquina, para dar continuidad al feliz presente del Sabadell, imbatido e invicto en LaLiga y campeón en la Copa Cataluña.

articles.title: Robert Lewandowski sends Champions League message to Barcelona
articles.summary: Robert Lewandowski has this week sent a message the way of former employers Barcelona, regarding the club’s ongoing pursuit of European glory.Frontman Lewand...
articles.body:
Robert Lewandowski has this week sent a message the way of former employers Barcelona, regarding the club's ongoing pursuit of European glory.

Frontman Lewandowski of course brought a close to his four-year stint in Blaugrana colours earlier this summer, following the expiration of his contract terms.

Across his spell in Catalunya's capital, the veteran goalscorer racked up three La Liga titles, the Copa del Rey, and a trio of Spanish Super Cups.

On the continent, however, Lewandowski and his teammates came up short time and again. This means that, all told, Barcelona have not lifted the Champions League since all the way back in 2015.

Speaking during an interview with Diario AS this week, the Pole was therefore drawn on the hopes of Hansi Flick's squad in Europe this coming season. And Lewandowski made use of the opportunity to explain:

"The Champions League is a dream for Barça. This season could be different from the previous one. Barça has a lot of quality players, as well as new signings. I hope they'll try to win the Champions League and be able to celebrate it."

articles.title: Cardale Jones, Ohio State national champion, joins Staples football staff as quarterbacks coach
articles.summary: Former Ohio State QB Cardale Jones has joined the Staples football staff. He led the Buckeyes to the 2014 national title.
articles.body:
Cardale Jones never envisioned being a football coach.

It's a title he's still trying to get used to after joining Matty Jacowleff's staff at Staples as quarterbacks coach this summer.

Part of the fun, of course, is when players find out about Jones' past, a history that features a national championship at Ohio State in 2014.

So how often do the players bring up the championship while working with Jones?

"Every day," Jones said with a laugh. "These guys are insane. They're relentless. Every day, it's another kid coming up to me and saying 'coach Jones, in my free period today, I looked you up on YouTube. I watched you play with this guy and that guy. Man, you were good.'

"I joke with them but honestly, that's what's helped with my transition there and my relationship with those guys. They're wide eyes and open ears and they're listening to every word I'm saying and trying to apply it immediately."

Staples officially announced Jones' addition to the coaching staff on Tuesday.

For Jacowleff, having a former national champ on the staff, someone with that kind of experience and history, has been a dream.

In fact, that's what the second-year Staples head coach thought it was at first.

"I go to bed very early, so I'm asleep by 9 p.m.," Jacowleff said. "I always wake up at like 11:30 p.m. I try not to check my phone, but I did this one night in June and I had a text from a number I didn't have saved and it read 'Hey coach this is Cardale Jones from Ohio State. I'm going to be in the area this summer. I would love it if we could connect.'"

Jacowleff woke up the next morning thinking "why did I have a dream that Cardale Jones texted me?"

The dream became reality, with a lot of miles in between for Jones.

The former Ohio State quarterback was drafted by the Bills in the fourth round of the 2016 NFL Draft, and also spent time with the Chargers and Seahawks before playing in the XFL, CFL and Indoor Football League.

Jones has a home in Columbus and a place in Stamford, and works as an analyst with CBS Sports in New York City.

He connected with the Staples football program while working with Brandon Gutman, who along with junior Grant Bozeman, is a contender for the starting quarterback job.

Jones estimated he's been at about 70% of the Wreckers' practices so far, and said he'll be at eight of the 10 regular-season games.

It has been a difficult offseason for Staples with quarterbacks coach Nick Chacho, 32, being diagnosed with stage 3 colon cancer during the winter. Jacowleff said the players and coaches have rallied behind Chacho and have held fundraisers.

"You talk about high school sports and high school football, and every team breaks it down to family, and we've got to be there for someone in our family when they need our help," Jacowleff said. "The most important thing to us was to put our team and our program in a position where we could support one of our own."

Jacowleff also spent time going to clinics, watching film and talking to mentors about quarterback play and technique so he could help Chacho at that position.

When Jacowleff was contacted by Jones, the former Ohio State QB wanted to make sure he was on the same page with the program.

"He wanted to sit down and talk through our playbook, the verbiage that we use, just to make sure that he's coaching in the same way that we coach," Jacowleff said. "He said 'if I'm doing this, I want to do a good job and do right by you guys as a team.'"

Then summer practices started, and Jones became more involved with the program and its plays.

"He always started our conversations with 'Are you open to feedback?'" Jacowleff said. "I'm sitting here going into my second year as a head coach and we have a former NFL quarterback and a national champion at Ohio State and he's offering feedback. I certainly could use that."

So far, it's been an ideal match for the program, the players and Jones, who is still getting acclimated to the title of coach.

"I've been liking every minute of it," Jones said. "Matty has done a great job at developing an unbelievable staff and I can't say enough great things about the kids. I never viewed myself as a coach. It's still funny getting used to them calling me coach. The kids are great, they're eager to learn, and they're respectful. I think that's what's making this process so enjoyable."

articles.title: Austin FC acquire Chris Applewhite on loan from Nashville SC
articles.summary: By Ari LiljenwallTRANSFER TRACKER STATUS: LoanATX receive: Chris ApplewhiteNSH receive: $50k GAMAustin FC have acquired defender Chris Applewhite on loan fro...
articles.body:
Austin FC have acquired defender Chris Applewhite on loan from Nashville SC , the clubs announced Wednesday.

The 19-year-old US youth international's loan is through June 2027 and includes a purchase option. In exchange, Nashville receive $50k in 2026 General Allocation Money (GAM).

"Chris is a highly rated prospect at the center back position and we're excited to welcome him to Austin," said Austin FC interim head coach Davy Arnaud. "He is coming off an excellent tournament with the U.S. U-20 team, and we hope to foster his continued development within our environment over the next year."

Applewhite joined Nashville as a homegrown player ahead of the 2025 season. He has made five MLS appearances (two starts), logging 188 minutes in league play.

At the international level, Applewhite recently captained the United States at the 2026 Concacaf U-20 Championship. They made the tournament final and qualified for the 2027 FIFA U-20 World Cup.

Austin are currently 14th in the Western Conference on 24 points, five points outside of an Audi MLS Cup Playoffs position. Nashville, meanwhile, lead the Supporters' Shield race with 52 points.

articles.title: Texas A&M football announces new midfield logo for Kyle Field
articles.summary: Texas A&M's Kyle Field will have a new look in 2026, with the Aggies announcing a new midfield logo ahead of the season.
articles.body:
Kyle Field will have a new midfield logo for the 2026 college football season, with the Texas A&M football program announcing the new design Wednesday.

They have gone much simpler, with the new midfield logo featuring a simple maroon TAM with a white outline and no bevel. The previous 50-yard design featured the Lone Star logo.

That is the only change they are making to Kyle Field, with both end zones still painted maroon and reading "TEXAS A&M" in white. The sidelines will continue to feature "G.R.I.N.D" and "HOME OF THE 12TH MAN" on each side.

The announcement comes as the Aggies prepare for their season opener against the Missouri State Bears on Saturday at Kyle Field in College Station. The game is set to start at 6 p.m. CT and will be on ESPN.

Head coach Mike Elko and Texas A&M are entering the season looking to not just make it back to the College Football Playoff after making their first appearance last season, but to win it all.

"We understand in this building that we have an opportunity to go compete for this thing… Now you have to go do it. This season is a long journey," Elko said in a recent interview . "We're excited that we have a team that we feel like can go compete for an opportunity to win the whole thing."

articles.title: Pau Quesada muestra su 'flow': "Tenemos una plantilla para ganar a cualquier equipo"
articles.standfirst: El técnico del Real Madrid se mostró feliz por el arranque de temporada de su equipo
articles.summary: El técnico del Real Madrid se mostró feliz por el arranque de temporada de su equipo
articles.body: Pau Quesada se mostró contento tras la clasificación del Real Madrid para la fase Liga de la Champions League. El técnico valenciano repitió en varias ocasiones la palabra flow para definir el estado de su equipo. "Tengo la plantilla que quería, tanto por los fichajes que ha realizado el club como por las incorporaciones de jugadoras del filial. Es una plantilla que combina esa juventud que nos dan esas cinco jugadoras que suben de la fábrica, más gente como Bella, Linda o Felicia, que son muy jóvenes, y se complementa con gente como Merle, Däbritz o Beernsteyn, que vienen de fuera. Tenemos ese mix de juventud y veteranía perfecto. Creo que tenemos una plantilla en la cual podemos optar a ganar a cualquier equipo", expuso. Felicia Schröder es el fichaje más caro en la historia del Real Madrid, una jugadora que el club tenía en su punto de mira desde hace meses. "Teníamos el target muy claro desde enero. Era la futbolista que queríamos. Tuvimos algún meeting con ella en el cual le planteamos nuestra idea futbolística. Detectamos su ilusión, su energía y sus ganas de venir al Real Madrid. Es una futbolista que nos aporta muchísima movilidad, que te da continuidad, pero a la vez te amenaza constantemente la espalda de los rivales. Es una rematadora, una delantera muy completa", explicó el técnico. "Ha empezado la temporada muy eficaz, anotando, y también a nivel defensivo presionando muchísimo y es la primera que también transmite eso. Así que hay que ayudarla para que siga en este estado de flow", añadió. Quesada insistió en la combinación fichajes, veteranía y juventud para confeccionar una plantilla con amplio fondo de armario. "Creo que una cosa que hemos hecho muy positiva en el mercado es que todos los perfiles de arriba se compenetran y se van complementando entre ellas porque cuando una viene al pie la otra va al espacio y cuando una se la queda la otra ataca. Y a partir de ahí tienen algo en común, que son muy agresivas en la presión y eso también refuerza la identidad del equipo. Yo creo que esa revolución de mercado también, aparte de lo que hemos ido a afirmar fuera, refuerza a nuestra cantera porque suben cinco jugadoras que están absolutamente preparadas, como se vio el otro día", aseveró. "A mí me ilusiona muchísimo lo que tengo de lunes a sábado en Valdebebas porque las veo entrenar. Hay una buena relación entre ellas, con el staff, con el club que está en el día a día también muy cerca de nosotros y es un estado de flow en el día a día muy positivo. Lo que tenemos que hacer como staff es darle las herramientas para que los resultados vayan acompañando, vayan sumando y que veamos un gran Real Madrid este año", destacó. Sobre el triunfo ante el Ajax en el Di Stéfano, con un gol de Linda Caicedo sobre la bocina, Pau dijo que "hemos entrado muy bien. Creo que los primeros 15 minutos han sido muy buenos y hemos estado cerca de adelantarnos. A partir de ahí creo que se ha notado un poco el cansancio, hemos ajustado en el descanso un par de situaciones y ha empezado a entrar gente del banquillo que nos ha dado esa frescura para poder volver a ser agresivas y dinámicas. Un partido que es 2-1, pero yo creo que hemos generado más ocasiones para que el resultado no fuera tan corto. Estamos contentos y toca felicitar a las jugadoras y al club porque un año más estamos en la fase Liga de Champions"

articles.title: Chilling plot to kidnap Kylian Mbappé and 25 other wealthy figures uncovered by French police, reports say
articles.summary: Football News: French authorities uncover a shocking kidnapping plot involving Kylian Mbappé and 25 other high-profile targets. Details emerge from a teenage suspect's seized mobile phones, revealing alarming plans and connections to a wider criminal organization.
articles.body: Kylian Mbappe was reportedly among 26 wealthy and high-profile individuals whose addresses and personal information were found by French investigators during an investigation into an alleged kidnapping plot. The Real Madrid and France star was said to have been one of several potential targets identified on mobile phones seized from an 18-year-old suspect who was allegedly continuing to run a criminal organisation from prison. The list reportedly also included a rapper, a Chinese businessman, jewellers and a Turkish meat trader.Mbappe among 26 alleged targetsAccording to French newspaper Le Parisien, investigators discovered the addresses of 26 wealthy individuals on two mobile phones seized from the 18-year-old suspect, identified as Clément L.Mbappe was reportedly among the names on the list, alongside a rapper and several wealthy businessmen. Those other alleged targets included a Chinese businessman, jewellers and a Turkish meat trader, with investigators reportedly finding information that could have been used to identify or locate them.The discovery came as authorities investigated the activities of the teenager, who allegedly continued directing a criminal organisation despite being held in prison.The case therefore concerns an alleged plot rather than a kidnapping that was carried out. Investigators are now seeking to determine how far the organisation had progressed, whether any of the potential targets were actually approached or monitored, and what each person under investigation allegedly did.Mbappe's inclusion is nevertheless particularly striking given his status as one of the most recognisable footballers in the world and his position as Real Madrid and France's captain.Suspect allegedly ran gang from his prison cellClément L was already in pre-trial detention in connection with allegations of pimping and organised robbery when investigators discovered that he was allegedly continuing to issue instructions from inside prison.According to Le Parisien, prison guards seized two mobile phones from him. Investigators then examined their contents and reportedly found information relating to the 26 alleged targets.The teenager was allegedly operating on Snapchat under the alias "Lester Z", using the phones to communicate and issue instructions to people outside the prison.A source close to the case told Le Parisien that the contents of the phones were particularly revealing."Two phones were seized by prison guards, and their contents were highly revealing," the source said.The same source added: "He also wanted to go after a rapper and the footballer Kylian Mbappe."The investigation reportedly began after authorities were looking into a separate robbery at a luxury watch shop in Neuilly-sur-Seine last April.Clément L had already been identified as one of two men allegedly involved in the attack on the watchmaker, which had led to his detention over armed robbery.The discovery of the phones subsequently opened a much wider line of investigation into the alleged criminal organisation and its potential plans.What happened when the teenager was questioned?During questioning, Clément L reportedly rejected the suggestion that he was the mastermind behind the alleged operation.He also asked to be released from solitary confinement, but that request was refused and he was ordered to remain there while the investigation continues.The teenager reportedly dropped out of school during the first year of a vocational qualification in cooking. He told investigators that he wanted to resume his education and eventually become a chef.Despite those claims about his future plans, he remains in pre-trial detention as authorities investigate the much more serious allegations surrounding the criminal organisation.His alleged accomplice has meanwhile been released under judicial supervision. That individual was challenging the measure on Wednesday before the Versailles investigating chamber.The investigation must now establish precisely how the alleged kidnapping operation was organised, how much preparation had taken place and whether the information found on the seized phones translated into concrete plans against any of the 26 people named.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.standfirst: El ex delantero culé atiende a Radio MARCA en el programa 'Otra Ronda'
articles.summary: El ex delantero culé atiende a Radio MARCA en el programa 'Otra Ronda'
articles.body: Robert Lewandowski ya mira hacia adelante, pero Barcelona sigue teniendo un lugar especial en su corazón. El delantero polaco, que este verano puso punto final a una etapa de cuatro temporadas en el conjunto azulgrana para emprender una nueva aventura en el Chicago Fire, atendió a Radio MARCA en una entrevista con Carlos Vicente ‘Chitu’, presentador de ‘Otra Ronda’, en el que se convirtió en uno de los padrinos del programa durante su tercer programa en antena. El encuentro tuvo lugar en Los Ángeles, donde Lewandowski presentó su propio modelo de los coches en miniatura de Hot Wheels, inspirado en su personalidad y en su trayectoria. Una cita muy especial para el delantero, que reconoció guardar todavía algunos de estos coches de su infancia. “Fueron para mí cuatro años muy bonitos en Barcelona. Pero hay un momento que tienes que hacer otra cosa, un nuevo paso, y ahora estoy muy contento”, explicó Lewandowski a Chitu. El polaco reconoció que necesita todavía algo de tiempo para adaptarse a su nueva vida: “Es normal, no solo porque me vaya de Europa, sino también porque voy a Estados Unidos”. El delantero no ocultó la nostalgia por su etapa en el Barça. “No soy un hombre muy emotivo, más bien frío, pero sí es un momento que siempre estoy para apoyar y ayudar al FC Barcelona y a mis excompañeros”, aseguró. Lewandowski llegó al Barcelona en 2022 y, durante sus cuatro temporadas en el club, conquistó tres Ligas y se proclamó Pichichi. Ahora, desde la distancia, sigue pendiente de lo que sucede en el conjunto azulgrana. “Estoy ahora mirando lo que pasó y estoy seguro de que voy a ganar muchos partidos”, afirmó, dejando claro que su nueva aventura en Estados Unidos no le hace perder de vista a su antiguo equipo. Preguntado por si al Barça le resultará sencillo olvidar sus goles, el polaco respondió con naturalidad: “Toda mi carrera quería jugar a mi nivel, siempre quería marcar goles y ayudar a mi equipo”. También recordó el contexto complicado que encontró a su llegada a Barcelona y destacó la evolución del club: “No era fácil al principio, pero luego creo que ahora es un club que está haciendo el próximo paso”. Y aunque ya no forma parte de la plantilla, Lewandowski mantiene un deseo: “Espero que al final pueda también celebrar con Barcelona unos títulos”. Durante la entrevista, Chitu también quiso conocer la opinión de Lewandowski sobre Rodri, al que se está señalando como uno de los grandes candidatos a ser considerado el mejor futbolista del mundo después del próximo Mundial. El polaco no dudó en elogiar al centrocampista español. “Es un jugador que sabe lo que necesita el equipo, cómo jugar hacia delante, pero también cómo jugar un poquito más en defensa. Es una experiencia que creo que este equipo necesita”, explicó. “Es un jugador que no solo en la Copa del Mundo, sino que desde hace muchos años está jugando al nivel superior”, añadió. La entrevista se produjo durante la presentación del Hot Wheels diseñado junto a Lewandowski. El coche está personalizado con los colores de Polonia, el número del delantero, su firma y uno de sus gestos más reconocibles tras marcar un gol. “Soy polaco, soy de Polonia, y si estás mirando los colores es como blanco y rojo. Para mí es algo especial”, explicó. El modelo también incluye detalles relacionados con su celebración después de marcar. Una elección con un componente especialmente emotivo para el delantero, que recordó su relación con Hot Wheels desde pequeño. “Al final estoy muy contento, es un sueño. Tenías un Hot Wheels cuando eras pequeñito y estás en un evento en Los Ángeles con tu coche de Hot Wheels. Es algo especial”, reconoció. Así terminó una entrevista especialmente simbólica: la primera de Lewandowski en una radio española tras dejar el Barcelona, y además con ‘Otra Ronda’ como escenario de su nueva etapa, convirtiéndose en uno de los padrinos del programa de Radio MARCA.

articles.title: Wrexham news: Parkinson pleased to see transfer window close
articles.summary: Phil Parkinson admits he is pleased the summer transfer window has closed and says Wrexham's 3-0 win at Millwall highlights the progress his side have made.
articles.body:
Phil Parkinson says he is pleased that the summer transfer window has closed as his Wrexham side ignited their campaign with a 3-0 victory over Millwall.

Striker Kieffer Moore and summer signing Jacques Ekomie both netted after Zak Sturge's first-half own goal as the Red Dragons won in style in the English capital .

Five of the Red Dragons' seven summer additions featured in the triumph over the Lions.

And having clinched a first Championship win of the season, Parkinson hopes his side can now kick-on amid some uncertainty within his squad during the latter stages of the window.

"I'm pleased the transfer window has closed, I've got to be honest with you," he said.

"I'm very pleased with the lads we've just brought in, Joe [Worrall] and Callum [O'Hare], I think they're two really good signings for us. They'll fit in really well with how we want to play.

"But in that last week of the window, there's uncertainty, people looking over their shoulders at who is coming in, people are thinking 'am I going to go?'.

"We had players who were close to leaving, so I'm just pleased it's closed and we can focus on the group."

Midfielder Lee leaves Wrexham by mutual consent

Coady with Liverpool U21s after Wrexham exit

Neither side managed a shot on target in the opening half at The Den, although Wrexham went ahead on 28 minutes as Issa Kabore's cross was deflected into the Millwall net by Sturge.

Wales international Moore added his side's second with a stunning 20-yard strike shortly after half-time before left wing-back Ekomie completed the rout with his first goal for the club.

"We won here last year, and that was a strong performance, but I think today was a performance of far more quality," added Parkinson.

"It showed where the team has progressed to. These are a good side, Millwall, they're a hard team to play at home and away.

"I thought we controlled the game for long periods tonight."

Moore's strike was his second of the campaign following his goal in the 1-1 draw with his former club Cardiff City on the opening weekend of the season.

Boss Parkinson was full of praise for the 34-year-old following his pivotal role in the Red Dragons' triumph over Alex Neil's outfit.

"Kieffer was good, wasn't he?" Parkinson added.

"He's up against three 6ft 5in centre-backs. That's tough. He gets battered from pillar to post.

"But he kept the ball, his ball retention was really good and he deserved that goal today."

articles.title: Kilmarnock 0-1 St Mirren: Killie remain without a point after loss to high-flying visitors
articles.summary: Report as St Mirren win 1-0 at Kilmarnock; Fraser Taylor's maiden goal for the visitors helped them to their first league win at Rugby Park in over 13 years; however, the pressure is increasing on struggling Kilmarnock
articles.body:
Saints passed up numerous opportunities during the first half but found themselves under pressure late on as Neil McCann's men chased an equaliser.

The Killie boss made three changes to his defence in response to their 4-0 home defeat to Dundee United last weekend.

Having conceded 13 goals in their opening three Premiership games, it was perhaps little surprise that McCann opted for a change of formation in an attempt to shore up his leaky backline.

Moving away from a back four to a 3-5-2, McCann brought in Erik Ring, George Stanger and Johnly Yfeko. The injured Robbie Deas and Nicky Clescenco dropped out, while Jonathan Meier was named on the bench.

There was one switch for the Buddies, with Taylor making his first league start of the new campaign in place of Samuel Ramos.

Joe Hugill almost found himself through on goal in the third minute when Max Stryjek's long pass caught out the St Mirren backline - but the striker was unable to bring the ball under control.

Killie were behind a minute later when the visitors pounced on some slack play in the middle of the park, launching a quick counter which ended with Taylor sweeping Nikolas Agrafiotis' pass into the bottom corner.

There was a nervousness around the home supporters any time Saints entered the final third.

On 13 minutes, an intricate passing move cut open the Killie defence, though Calvin Ramsay's strike deflected off Yfeko and against the right-hand post.

Just after the half-hour mark, another smart block from Yfeko prevented Chris Mochrie from doubling Saints' lead.

The resulting corner also caused problems in the home defence, though this time Declan John was unable to take advantage as he slashed well wide of the target.

Paul Nsio was next to try his luck for Craig McLeish's side, sending an angled effort high and wide in the final minute of the first half.

Following another abject display from his team, McCann made a triple substitution at half-time. Jamie Brandon, Aaron Tshibola and Djenairo Daniels came on for Tyreece John-Jules, Yfeko and Ring.

Jacob Chapman was tested for the first time in the 47th minute when he batted away Tom Lowery's free-kick.

On the hour mark, the St Mirren keeper comfortably gathered Michael Schjonning-Larsen's low drive as the driving rain continued to batter Rugby Park.

With the home side pressing for an equaliser, they were leaving big gaps at the back which St Mirren looked to exploit at every opportunity.

A well-worked counter saw Jake Young combine well with Nsio, but the forward couldn't quite adjust his feet in order to get a shot away.

Killie responded quickly at the other end with a promising attack of their own. However, Daniels was unable to profit as Chapman raced from his goal, with the substitute instead sending the ball into the side netting.

With 17 minutes remaining, a brave block by Alex Gogic kept out Rory McKenzie's goal-bound volley.

In the final minute, Cathal McCarthy nodded into the side-netting from close range after finding room inside the box at a corner.

Despite their improvements in the second half, chances were limited for Killie, ensuring Saints picked up a rare three points in Ayrshire.

"The first half was excellent, I thought some of the stuff we played was great.

"I'm probably just a bit disappointed that we didn't add more to it.

"I wanted the second half to look exactly like the first half, but we know there's going to be spells in games where we suffer without the ball at times.

"I probably need to get more comfortable in those situations because I just want us to have the ball all the time.

"It's our third clean sheet in the league which is ultimately the foundation of what our success needs to be built on.

"You have to be tough to play against in this league, we built success in recent times by being tough to play against, we just didn't score enough goals.

"Someone said it was our first league win at Rugby Park in quite some time.

"We're coming away to tough venues, from the start of the game we showed probably the best version of what we want to be.

"The boys will get frustrated at me because I want that for 90 minutes, keep asking them for more and trying to raise their standards - they are raising the bar every single week."

"I actually feel for the players if I'm being honest.

"After four minutes, you are 1-0 down again and you can feel the tension within the stadium.

"It's not what we want or what we work on, you can almost see them for that little part after the goal going into a shell - that's understandable.

"I felt we gathered ourselves and completely dominated the second half without really showing our quality.

"This has been a difficult start, after four league games we've not got any points yet.

"But I know there's enough in that dressing room that once it clicks, and I know it will click, we'll start motoring."

articles.title: Motherwell 3-0 Dundee United: Well continue unbeaten league start with stroll against visitors
articles.summary: Report as Motherwell beat Dundee United 3-0; goals from Seb Palmer-Houlden, Alex Lowry and Dylan Levitt helped Well maintain their unbeaten start to the Scottish Premiership season; visitors suffered a third loss in four games
articles.body:
Goals from Seb Palmer-Houlden, Alex Lowry and Dylan Levitt helped Well maintain their unbeaten start to the Scottish Premiership season while United suffered a third loss in four games.

Alfred Johansson's side were aided by the 14th-minute straight red card for Emmanuel Agyei which ensured the Tangerines' dismal winless run at Fir Park, which stretches back to April 2023, continued.

The hosts slipped into attack mode from the first whistle.

A typically slick surge down the right punctured United's backline and Joe Hodge drilled in a low cross which Lowry met first time, only for his shot to be superbly beaten out by goalkeeper Jack Walton before Emmanuel Longelo followed up to crack an effort against a post.

It was a sign of things to come and a stark warning for the Tannadice side as they rode their luck after twice failing to match runners into the box.

The visitors were screaming for a penalty when Mehdi Merghem tumbled inside the box under a Lukas Fadinger challenge but referee Callum Scott turned a deaf ear to their pleas.

Palmer-Houlden was next to be given time and space to fire in a low shot which Walton was again able to deal with but United's backline was living on its nerves.

A reckless lunge from Agyei on Lowry saw United reduced to 10 men and it got worse moments later as the hosts opened the scoring.

Tom Sparrow was the provider with a cut-back from the right which was buried by Palmer-Houlden with a low finish from a tight angle.

United began to buckle under relentless Motherwell attacking surges and it required acrobatics from Walton to prevent Fadinger from finding the top corner on the half-hour mark.

A brilliant 25-yarder from Lowry in the 65th minute added a second for Well and former United midfielder Levitt made it three with a low shot from distance two minutes later.

It completed a miserable night for Jim Goodwin's men, who never recovered from their numerical disadvantage during another eye-catching display from the hosts who could have inflicted far heavier damage.

"We looked patient, but with tempo on the ball. I think 700 passes, even playing against 10 men for so long, that's quite a lot of passes, which suggests the tempo of the passing game was high and I'm pleased with that. So then, if you play well, the goals will come.

"I'm pleased with the focus of the players and obviously with the result, which could have been even bigger so I'm very pleased.

"I think Joe Hodge deserved so much credit too. He, I think, probably played his best game for Motherwell, giving so much fluidity to our in-possession faces and so intense in the defensive transitions. He was very good for the team.

"We had three new players scoring and it's good for them to check that box but it's more important to be able to stay calm and focus on what they have to do on the pitch, which is more important than them thinking about scoring."

Dundee United assistant boss Lee Sharp :

"I thought we started the game well, both teams kind of going at it for the first 10-12 minutes, and after that it becomes extremely difficult when you're down to 10 men for that length of time.

"It kind of killed the game. I thought the boys were excellent in terms of how they went about it. They worked tirelessly in there but it was just disappointing.

"Motherwell are a good footballing team, so they'll just keep the ball and make you look to get it back, which the boys have done. We still played at times when we did get it, but it was extremely difficult.

"We'll review the red card and we'll make a decision going forward from there. Obviously, if the footage shows that you might think you've got a case, given how important Emmanuel is, we'll look at it and see."

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Burnley 1-1 Middlesbrough: Ugo Raghouber earns point for Clarets
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Burnley and Middlesbrough at Turf Moor on Wednesday; Ugo Raghouber strikes equaliser as Clarets hit back to earn a much-needed point.
articles.body:
The French midfielder, signed from Lille in July, steered in a 54th-minute equaliser after taking on Zeki Amdouni's pass and being allowed to run unchallenged.

Aidan Morris had swept Middlesbrough into a 23rd-minute lead, scoring his first goal after more than two years at the club, with a stylish finish from 20 yards after being set up by fellow American Sebastian Berhalter.

For Burnley, the point was a lift after a testing week.

Head coach Nicky Hayen, whose side were beaten 4-1 at Norwich last Saturday, had to rethink his attack after last season's top scorer Zian Flemming was sold to Ipswich for £20million late on transfer deadline day, and decided to bring in Andreas Hountondji - out on loan for the past season and a half - in for his first Clarets start since November 2024.

Middlesbrough might have gone ahead as early as the third minute when leading scorer Will Lankshear sprinted on to a long pass from goalkeeper Radek Vitek that caught Burnley defender Hjalmar Ekdal ball watching, but could only bundle the ball wide as home stopper Max Weiss closed in on him.

Vitek had to be alert on the quarter-hour mark to push away a 20-yard shot from Dastan Satpayev, the Chelsea loanee making his home debut, who had created the opening after exchanging passes with Amdouni.

But it was Middlesbrough who struck first through Morris, one of four Americans now at the club. The delighted travelling support greeted the goal with the chants of 'USA, USA' that have become familiar at their games this season.

The match had a physical edge to it, with Vitek angry after being caught by Satpayev as he chased a back pass, and Lankshear booked for treading on Hannibal Mejbri's foot.

Morris almost added a second Middlesbrough goal two minutes before half-time following a loose Connor Roberts clearance, striding forward and smashing a shot against Weiss' left-hand post from 25 yards.

Then Lankshear slipped past Anel Ahmedhodzic after Kyle Joseph flicked Adilson Malanda's pass into his path, and crossed low for Riley McGree to steer wide on the stretch from six yards.

But Burnley improved after half-time and drew level when Raghouber guided a shot into the corner from just outside the penalty area.

Then the impressive Satpayev ran at Alfie Jones and twisted inside the Middlesbrough centre-back, his sliding shot being stopped by the trailing leg of the wrongfooted Vitek.

Substitute Aaron Ramsey fired just wide with 12 minutes left as Burnley chased a winner, but they had to settle for a point.

"We started with good intentions in the first 10 minutes. But then they scored the goal and then there was a certain fear in the team.

"We were dropping back. We were not putting pressure in the right way. That's something we changed in the second half.

"Then you see that we play with a lot more courage and then we felt after that goal with the support of the fans that you can change that game.

"But I have to be fair also, physically we're not there yet at the moment because we have also new signings who didn't have a proper pre-season, who didn't play a lot of friendly games."

"We were the better team from my point of view and controlled things, playing good football. We created a lot of chances, especially in the first half, and kept them to very few.

"They had a spell in the second half, maybe 15 minutes, where they were quite strong but didn't create so many chances.

"But sometimes we were not good enough with the ball, and Burnley got the crowd with them.

"Otherwise, I think it was a very good performance. We would have wanted three points, but we had to settle for one.

"We're still getting there with a lot of players coming back and we're building them up, which means we will just get better. But I think this was a big step forward in terms of how we want to look as a football side.

"I think this, in general, was one of our best performances this season in terms of how we looked against very strong opponents."

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: West Bromwich Albion 1-1 Charlton Athletic: Tyreece Campbell scores to earn point for Addicks
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between West Bromwich Albion and Charlton Athletic at The Hawthorns on Wednesday; Tyreece Campbell cancels out Callum Styles' opener to earn a point for the unbeaten Addicks.
articles.body:
Nathan Jones' side were looking to continue their blistering start to the campaign - but spent the majority of the game on the back foot against the Baggies.

They frustrated the home side who finally broke the deadlock with a thunderous Callum Styles strike just before the hour mark.

But having soaked up waves of pressure - Campbell fired home from close range after 69 minutes to earn a point for his side.

It was Albion who had the upper hand over the high flying Addicks in the opening 20 minutes at The Hawthorns.

Felix Horn Myhre headed over after just two minutes before Callum Styles tried his luck from range.

Ousmane Diakite saw a shot deflected wide after good work from lively full debutant Kareem Tunde, who was causing problems for the visitors on the right flank.

He pulled a shot wide from distance on the 20-minute mark, while Isaac Price tested Charlton shot stopper Arthur Okonkwo, with Albion dominating possession.

But despite having more of the ball and a handful of half chances - the Baggies were struggling to turn their territory into clear-cut opportunities against a resilient Charlton back line.

The second period began in much the same fashion as Price saw an effort flash wide just seconds after the restart - with Albion flying back out of the blocks.

Albion had Charlton camped in their own quarter, but again they were holding firm. It felt like the Baggies were going to need something special to break the Addicks' rearguard, and so it proved after 59 minutes.

After half-time substitute Rabby Nzingoula had drawn a top save out of Okonkwo, Styles ended a 16-month wait for a goal as he rifled home from 18 yards out, after Charlton failed to clear a Price corner.

It was exactly what Albion deserved but having dominated possession and restricted Charlton to nothing by way of chances - Jones' side levelled 10 minutes later with their first shot on target.

They countered down the left and Miles Leaburn headed substitute Ivan Mesik's cross into the path of Campbell - who fired home through a crowd of bodies to land Albion with a sucker punch.

Up to that point Charlton had hardly troubled the home side - but they somehow found themselves on level terms.

After the goal sparked a spell of pressure from the visitors, it was Albion who were again back on the front foot heading into the final throes of the game.

But they could not find an equaliser and were left to settle for a frustrating point.

"I'm frustrated we didn't win the game to be honest. We were really good in the first half and lacked that last little bit.

"At half time it was a case of we have got them where we want them, we're tiring them out and we just need to kick it up a level.

"We did that and they have one opportunity where they get into the box and it ends up in our goal.

"When we are dominant and they are not getting a kick, we need to not let them get in and around the box, or stop the cross.

"They are good at what they do, and proved that by picking up the results they have, but we have to be better around the box.

"But in a short period of time we have come a long way, especially having brought in a lot of new signings who are finding their feet, so that is positive."

"We are on that trajectory with what we did at Luton during my two spells there.

"We built a team to go through the leagues, I went and then came back and built a team that was on the brink of promotion and got promoted.

"We are on that trajectory, after four games we are in a good place, and let's not mess about, we are favourites to go down.

"Not one of the favourites, we are the favourites and people are saying they can't sustain it, but that is fine.

"We gave the ball away too much at times in the first half and were not brave enough.

"After they scored and we made subs, we were much better and got back into it. It's optimistic to say we should have gone on to win it, but we did finish strongly and it is a great point."

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Dundee 1-1 St Johnstone: Saints secure Tayside derby draw after late drama at Dens Park
articles.summary: Report as Dundee and St Johnstone draw 1-1 at Dens Park; the Dark Blues looked to have sealed all three points when substitute Charlie Reilly netted in the 87th minute; Saints sub Josh Fowler responded in the 90th minute to ensure the visitors avoided a third straight league loss
articles.body:
After a goalless, lacklustre first half shaded by the visitors, the Dark Blues looked to have sealed all three points when substitute Charlie Reilly netted in the 87th minute.

But Saints sub Josh Fowler responded in the 90th minute to ensure the visitors avoided a third straight Scottish Premiership defeat.

The hosts made three changes to the team that lost to Hibernian on Sunday with Brad Halliday, Bobby Wales and Alan Forrest coming in for Drey Wright, Bradley Fink and Reilly.

Shortly before kick-off, Dundee announced the signing of Jack Moorhouse on a season-long loan from Manchester United but he was not in the matchday squad.

Saints made two alterations to the side that was beaten by Hearts at Tynecastle on Saturday with Fowler and Liam Smith making way for Matty Todd and Taylor Steven.

St Johnstone were the first to threaten in the sixth minute when Enes Alic cut the ball back from the right to Steven who hit a sweet strike that was pushed for a corner by home goalkeeper Owen Goodman.

Dundee's first chance arrived 13 minutes later. Saints keeper Toby Steward came to punch a cross with home striker Joe Westley getting his head to it first but the ball bounced just past the post.

Steven had the ball in the net just before the half-hour mark but the goal was ruled out for an earlier infringement.

As the half drew to a close, the Perth side pinned Dundee back with Goodman having to look lively to keep out a deflected Sam Stanton shot.

Dundee finally created their first big opportunity of the game in the 60th minute when Westley was sent clean through on goal but his low shot from just inside the Saints box flew past Steward's left-hand post.

Saints finally threatened in the 64th minute with Kai Fotheringham coming off the bench and shortly after he sent a curling strike just wide.

Dundee hit back with Westley having a half chance inside the Saints box but Steward made a vital block, sending the ball out for a corner.

Further home pressure saw the ball fall kindly for Reilly but his composure deserted him and he blasted well over.

However, the winger made no mistake in the 87th minute. A looping header from Westley cannoned off the crossbar and Reilly was first to react to nod the ball home.

That seemed to be that but Saints dug out another chance in the 90th minute with Fowler smashing a shot on the turn past the helpless Goodman to secure a point.

"St Johnstone had the greater percentage of possession. I thought that we had the bigger chances within the game.

"Overall, the draw was a true reflection of the game.

"But obviously, after scoring so late on, we hoped we'd see the game out.

"I was happy with some aspects of the performance but there was a recurring theme from the last couple of games.

"We need to improve in possession. We need to have more sustained periods controlling the game. We surrendered possession too often.

"We are a danger on the counter-attack but we also have got to get a little bit better on controlling games and sustaining the pressure.

"At home, we obviously always want to win games of football. You never know in football just how important that point would be.

"We always respond positively to setbacks like the one at the weekend.

"But we're disappointed when we took the lead not to see the game through."

"We had lost two matches and some moments of those two matches we have performed very, very well.

"So to come here and to play as we did tonight, I am very pleased for our players.

"They showed the character to play in this pressure environment in a local derby against a good opponent.

"We are a little bit different to how we were last year but I know the players never ever give up.

"They pushed until the end and we deservedly got our goal.

"We will take that one point in an away match and now we will recover."

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Georgia AG Calls for LSU's Removal from SEC if it Violates Rules amid Lane Kiffin Comments
articles.summary: Georgia is prepared to remove LSU from the SEC if it violates rules regarding former NFL players.
articles.body:
Georgia is prepared to remove LSU from the SEC if it violates rules regarding former NFL players.

The state's attorney general, Chris Carr, wrote a letter to SEC commissioner Greg Sankey Wednesday encouraging the SEC "to take all measures available to address this conduct, up to and including suspension and/or removing LSU from the Conference," per ESPN's Mark Schlabach and Pete Thamel .

"Conference members have the freedom to associate with institutions committed to following NCAA and Conference rules," Carr wrote. "No institution should be allowed to ignore the obligations of Conference membership while continuing to receive the benefits of membership."

Last week, the SEC announced that it intends to prohibit athletes from returning to member schools from pro teams after former Cleveland Browns tight end Dae'Quan Wright committed to play for LSU . A Texas judge issued an order overruling the SEC's decision.

Kiffin, who is also attempting to roster defensive lineman Zxavian Harrison and edge-rusher Junior Tuihalamaka, told Thamel that he's been in "daily communication" with the conference, adding that the rule "does not prohibit players from practicing at the school, it prohibits them from being added to the final 105 roster, which has to be turned in on Friday."

Kiffin also said this week that his players are in favor of adding former NFL players to the roster.

"Every one of them was emphatic about, 'If they can help us win, bring 'em,'" he told reporters . "We understand we have a team that's practiced together and worked together all offseason, but one of them said, 'Hey, this is how it works at the next level, and this is how the real world works.' So that made me feel a little better in the struggle and being torn back and forth."

On Tuesday, Tennessee chancellor Donde Plowman, who is also the president of the SEC's executive committee, said the league "will not budge" on its ruling on NFL players returning to SEC rosters. She added that the SEC is "prepared to defend our rules" and will back Sankey in doling out penalties to schools that violate the rules.

"We have a responsibility to try and lead the best we can in this time of chaos," Plowman told ESPN . "Our group is united on this. This is not a rule we will budge on... Enough is enough."

LSU has yet to formally sign a former NFL player to its roster, but should the Tigers bring in a former pro player, it appears it could lead to a legal battle. Kiffin must finalize his roster 24 hours before the Tigers' season opener against Clemson on Saturday.

articles.title: Falkirk 1-2 Rangers: Lawrence Shankland's double secures Scottish Premiership victory against winless Bairns
articles.summary: Report and highlights as Rangers win at Falkirk; Lawrence Shankland's stunning strike gave Rangers the lead; Kosta Nedeljkovic's own goal pulled the hosts level; Shankland secured the win late on; the Ibrox side have won back-to-back league games; the Bairns remain winless
articles.body:
Manager Derek McInnes was forced to watch from the stand at a rainy Falkirk Stadium as he began his touchline ban for comments made last season while in charge of Hearts.

It was his former Jambos captain who gave them the lead in style, collecting Djeidi Gassama's ball and smashing it into the net after eight minutes.

They were far from convincing and Kosta Nedeljkovic inexplicably knocked the ball into his own net to pull the Bairns level before half-time.

Falkirk then had the better of the chances and Jacob Murrell should have put them ahead on his home debut.

Aodhan Doherty wasted a brilliant chance after a mix-up between Gers keeper Ivor Pandur and Ross McCrorie, with the substitute then setting up his captain to sweep in the winner late on.

John McGlynn's remain without a league win and are only above pointless Kilmarnock, while Rangers are fifth on seven points from their four matches.

The key moments from the Falkirk Stadium

8: GOAL! Brilliant from the Rangers captain. Gassama sends the ball into Shankland, he switches onto his left before firing into the net.

16: CHANCE! Ross feeds the ball through to Fodrey in the box, but he can't get his feet sorted.

19: OFF THE POST! Kim denied by the woodwork.

24: SAVE! Kim close again! Bain reacts quickly to deny the Rangers newcomer, Raskin hits the side netting with the rebound.

44: GOAL! Falkirk are level. Ross sends in a cross, Nedeljkovic slides in to try and clear but instead puts it past Pandur.

48: SAVE! Fodrey gets his head to a cross but it's plucked out the air by Pandur.

51: CHANCE! Ross with a brilliant cross to the feet of Murrell but his effort lacks power and Pandur saves.

52: WIDE! What a chance for Shankland. Curtis lays it on a plate for the Rangers skipper but he somehow puts it past.

61: OVER! A brilliant chance for the Bairns. Murrell's header is deflected over the bar.

62: CHANCE! Falkirk should be in front! Murrell is one-on-one with Pandur after an awful pass from Fernandez, but his shot lacks power and the opportunity is gone.

78: WHAT A MISS! Doherty should have the ball in the after a mix up between Pandur and Curtis, but he gets it all wrong.

79: GOAL! A huge goal from the captain. Shankland collects McCrorie's pass, takes a touch then fires into the bottom corner.

Former Rangers midfielder Scott Arfield on Sky Sports:

"At Hearts, Shankland had runners going in behind and I think you've got that now with this front four.

"Gassama looks like he's reinvented himself which obviously helps him and his two goals are just class.

"Shankland just touches it and he just knows where the goal is.

"It's like an easy wee golf shot and he just touches it, finishes it.

"Goals never move and he makes it look so easy and he'll continue to do that time and time and time again and that is why you bring him to the club because he is just a classy finisher."

"It's all about points to a certain point then you've got to start winning with performances.

"They've done enough to get over the line, but it's got to be better.

"It is all about winning but, at the same time, you've got to see signs of improvement and it was a slogfest out there for Rangers again.

"You're only as good as you're strikers and that's been the story tonight.

"You look at the chances Murrell missed at the other end, Rangers have got a clinical striker."

Rangers manager Derek McInnes speaking to Sky Sports:

"Too scrappy for my liking. There were too many opportunities in the game for Falkirk.

"Lack of concentration in what you're trying to do really. If you're going to play the ball at the back and bring teams onto you it's to try and go somewhere with it.

"I just thought we ran up a cul-de-sac and gave away a few stupid little fouls. Just invites pressure and gives them a bit of encouragement.

"Sometimes that's where experience comes in.

"I'm not unhappy because we've won the game and we're in the back of winning at Aberdeen on Sunday.

"It's great to get another three points. I thought the effort for the team was great. As a team it was great.

"All the characteristics you want for a team coming away from home were there.

"It's all about winning games and hopefully now we can move on to Saturday and two home games now for us to look forward to.

"The window will be closed when we come into that game. I think that will be a godsend for me and for everybody else here."

Rangers captain Lawrence Shankland speaking to Sky Sports:

"Delighted to follow up from the weekend with another good result.

"We had quite a lot of moments around their box and I think we just snatched at a couple of things and made the wrong decisions.

"We knew we had to tidy up in the final third. I'll just keep shooting with my left foot!

"The scrutiny is up there at the moment, but I just had to stay confident and another chance would come.

"There's been a lot to sort out and take in. When you start winning games, it breeds confidence and everything feels a bit easier.

"We know we've got a lot to improve on with our performances, but we had some good moments and we'll take those positives."

Falkirk manager John McGlynn speaking to Sky Sports:

"Absolutely gutted for the players, they put so much into the game to not get anything from it.

"We don't want to be known as the team who can play some nice football but not come out with points. We had some good opportunities in the second half that could have got us into a lead.

"I'm proud of the players for the performance they've put on and the effort they've put into the game.

"We go to Celtic Park and come out with a bit of credit, we get credit tonight but we want to get points out these games.

"We need to start winning games, but with the performance we have the encouragement that will come."

articles.title: Man City transfer news: New midfield but major Haaland gamble
articles.summary: Manchester City have completed a squad overhaul including a fully revamped midfield to the tune of a Premier League record £458m, but that eyewatering number does not tell the full story.
articles.body:
Manchester City have completed their squad overhaul - including a fully revamped midfield - to the tune of £458m, a new Premier League record for a summer window.

But that eyewatering sum does not tell the full story.

New Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca received the full backing of director of football Hugo Viana in his first transfer window in charge after replacing Pep Guardiola. Indeed, City's record transfer fee was twice broken this summer.

A joint-British record £125m was spent on Maresca's former Chelsea skipper Enzo Fernandez after £116m was committed on Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest . Morocco international Ayyoub Bouaddi, 18, was also brought in for £86m. The trio accounted for the bulk of City's summer incomings.

The departures of captain Bernardo Silva, 2024 Ballon d'Or winner Rodri, Tijjani Reijnders and Nico Gonzalez means the City midfield has been completely transformed.

Senior club sources are said to be delighted by the business done not only during the past couple of months but in January too, when plans were brought forward to sign long-term targets Antoine Semenyo and Marc Guehi.

And if the clock is rewound further back, Manchester City 's rebuild of the team that won the 2023 Champions League really began in January 2025 after a difficult start to that season.

Just four players remain from the starting eleven and substitutes from the night they beat Inter Milan in Istanbul to win the continent's biggest club prize.

Maresca now has the luxury of calling upon two established players in almost every position. City feel the squad is stronger at this point than at the beginning of last season which they believe has been achieved by remaining calm and trusting the transfer strategy.

How will their new midfield signings all fit together?

And, despite the vast amount of money spent, have they actually left themselves without a back-up to Erling Haaland?

Deadlines, acrimony and a record as Man City back Maresca for Fernandez deal

Ndiaye's journey from non-league football to £65m Man City move

City's expenditure of £542m on new signings since the turn of the year will grab the headlines, but it often goes under the radar how well they do at selling fringe players.

During this same period, they have recouped £334m, including £75m for Savinho, who scored only two Premier League goals during his time at City, as well as £65m for Rodri and £52m for Reijnders.

It gives City a net spend of £208m in 2026, which will be further bolstered by Tottenham 's obligation to buy Omar Marmoush for £60m at the end of his loan spell next season.

Sources had said during the summer that they were operating on a one-out, one-in policy and Maresca managed to replace almost every player that departed, aside from Nico Gonzalez and Marmoush.

With the side well stocked at left-back, it is felt that Nico O'Reilly will play more in his natural midfield position to ease the Gonzalez gap.

The club believe the record fee for Fernandez is justified by acquiring a proven winner at the highest level that will strengthen the midfield. Anderson was the summer's number one target, while 18-year-old Bouaddi is seen as having all the attributes to develop into a world class talent.

City have won back-to-back games at the start of the Premier League season and Maresca will now have a selection dilemma each game as he possesses an embarrassment of riches to choose from.

The question is how the Italian will now fit them all together.

Analysis: How will Maresca use his new midfielders?

Fernandez, Bouaddi, and Anderson are all players comfortable across multiple positions in Maresca's system.

Maresca has moved between a box and a diamond shape in midfield at City. The main difference between the two shapes is that the former has two natural holding midfielders and the second a single holding midfielder.

Against Bournemouth , Guehi paired Anderson at the base of midfield. O'Reilly, the left-sided attacking midfielder, was joined by right-back Rico Lewis, moving in-field to form the box.

Against Crystal Palace , left-back Josko Gvardiol and attacking midfielder O'Reilly flanked number 10 Rayan Cherki as the three ahead of Anderson in what looked like a diamond.

Anderson anchoring the midfield suggests Maresca sees him as Rodri's successor.

While full of praise for Bouaddi, Maresca has stressed his youth, a nod to the fact that he will likely deputise for Anderson.

Bouaddi replaced Anderson against Palace and his short cameo came soon after the introduction of Mateo Kovacic. In pre-season, the Croatian appeared to be Maresca's first choice holding midfielder but has since slid down the pecking order.

When he came on, although starting higher than Bouaddi in the midfield diamond, he dropped deep to get on the ball in holding midfield. When this happened, Bouaddi took Kovacic's position higher up.

These rotations between holding midfield and central midfield are movements Maresca may also encourage Anderson to perform when others fill the space behind him.

Versatility in the midfield four is key. Fernandez, under Maresca, was capable of playing at the base of midfield or as an attacking midfielder on both sides.

The last midfield spot, the number 10 position, has been shared between Foden and Cherki. Although Foden did play right wing against Bournemouth and Palace given City's injuries, Maresca has spoken of his central quality.

Given Foden's promising showings as a box-to-box midfielder last season – there is also a possibility both him and Cherki play through the middle together at some point this season.

Despite the positives around the recent window, Haaland is now City's only first-team striker.

The 26-year-old is pivotal to the team, ending last season as the Premier League top scorer with 27 goals, and starting the new campaign by netting twice in as many games.

But should Haaland be unavailable, what are City's options?

Marmoush wanted to play regular first-team football and was allowed to join Tottenham , while 21-year-old Divin Mubama, who did well in pre-season, joined Championship side Southampton on loan.

City believe they have enough flexibility from within their options to have not directly replaced Marmoush.

Semenyo operates mainly from the right flank but is seen as an option at number nine, having played in the position during some cup games last season.

Deadline day signing Ndiaye is another who can operate there and the £60m forward adds greater versatility and squad depth as someone who is a proven Premier League player.

However, of the forward, attacking midfield and wide options, Semenyo is the only one to get into double figures in the Premier League in the last couple of seasons.

Cherki, Jeremy Doku and Ndiaye have never hit that mark, while Foden is clearly capable, having hit 19 Premier League goals in 2023-24, but has struggled for consistent form in the last two seasons

Unless a couple of those step up, it could be one to watch if Haaland either needs to be rested or gets injured.

articles.title: Lane Kiffin's LSU Reveals Custom Cleats in New Photos for CFB Season Opener vs. Dabo, Clemson
articles.summary: Lane Kiffin's LSU Tigers will wear custom cleats during a season-opening matchup with Dabo Swinney and Clemson on Saturday.
articles.body:
Lane Kiffin's LSU Tigers will wear custom cleats during a season-opening matchup with Dabo Swinney and Clemson on Saturday.

LSU showcased the cleats in a series of photos posted on X.

The Tigers are looking to start off strong under Kiffin, who will be coaching his first game since the school hired him as head coach in Nov. 2025.

LSU is coming off a disappointing 2025 campaign, finishing with a 7-6 record and losing to Houston in the Texas Bowl. The Tigers fired head coach Brian Kelly midway through the season.

LSU's roster looks vastly different under Kiffin, as the school compiled the No. 1 transfer portal class in the country during the 2026 cycle (via 247Sports' composite rankings ).

The new-look Tigers' first test will come against a Clemson squad that's also attempting to bounce back from a 7-6 finish last year, although Swinney's team previously made a College Football Playoff appearance in 2024.

Kickoff between LSU and Clemson on Saturday is at 7:30 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Washington Football's Defensive Line Headlined By Fresh Faces
articles.summary: While the Huskies starting defensive line features two standout freshmen, the depth and experience behind them will be the X-factor up front.
articles.body:
With the 2026 season finally upon us, one aspect of Washington's defense will feature a multitude of fresh faces. After seniors Zach Durfee and Anterio Thompson left and were selected in the 2026 NFL draft, the Huskies will replace the veterans with young, blue-chip talent.

That talent comes in the form of two of the highest-rated recruits in the state last year: defensive tackle Derek Colman-Brusa and edge rusher Ramzak Fruean, who are set to make their first career start in the Apple Cup against Washington State on Sunday, September 6.

Joining the youngsters up front will be a pair of fourth-year Huskies: tackle Elinneus Davis and outside linebacker Jacob Lane. Both Davis and Lane played in all 13 games for defensive coordinator Ryan Walters last season, and now, the experienced pass rushers can take the freshman duo under their wing.

Behind them, Walters has several new faces expected to make an impact in the rotation. Along the interior are Sacramento State transfer DeSean Watts, Ball State transfer Darin Conley, and Mississippi State transfer Kai McClendon. Although McClendon is recovering from an ACL injury sustained at Mississippi State, he was fully cleared for contact in the final week of fall camp.

The incoming trio has adapted nicely to Walters' system, which finished last year ranked No. 12 in the country in rushing yards allowed per game.

On the outside, there's a bit more familiarity with the scheme, as fifth-year seniors Isaiah Ward and Russell Davis II will back up Lane and Fruean. Although the former Arizona transfers have been productive when on the field, they have struggled with injuries since following Jedd Fisch to Seattle, with Ward missing five games last year and Davis II missing the entire season due to a knee injury.

Additionally, sophomore Devin Hyde and Ohio State transfer Logan George will provide depth along the edge. In his freshman season, Hyde played in all 13 games while totaling three tackles, one tackle for loss, and a sack. As for the former Buckeye, he played just 19 snaps in 2025 while limited by injury, but he led the Big Sky in 2024 with 16.5 tackles for loss.

The Huskies finished No. 84 in total sacks in 2025 with just 24, and with additional depth plus a healthy rotation heading into 2026, Walters' inventive scheming and play-calling will give his squad a chance to increase upon that total this season.

There's no questioning the wide range of experience up front for Walters' unit. It may take some time before a rotation is solidified, especially considering the multitude of players who have battled injuries throughout their careers and may need some time to get comfortable on the field.

However, with two of college football's most highly touted freshmen in the starting lineup, to go along with an influx of experienced transfers, the defensive front now has the talent and experience to piece together a destructive pass rush.

articles.title: 🚨 Historic signing! Rebeca Bernal joins Manchester United Women
articles.summary: The transfer market brought positive news for Mexico in women’s soccer, as this Wednesday Rebeca Bernal’s historic move to Manchester United was confirmed.Th...
articles.body:
The transfer market brought positive news for Mexico in women's soccer, as this Wednesday Rebeca Bernal's historic move to Manchester United was confirmed.

The former Monterrey player will be the first Mexican woman to play in England's Women's Super League, and what better way to do it than with one of the most important teams in the competition.

Bernal was part of Rayadas' multiple championship-winning squads from the creation of Liga MX Femenil in 2017 until 2025, when she received her first international opportunity with the Washington Spirit.

"Rebeca is an exceptional player who brings quality, leadership, and experience to our young and promising squad," said Matt Johnson, Director of Women's Football for the Red Devils.
